title: 2020_PMC7006828_Kansan_Guardian_Perceptions_of_HPV_and_the_HPV_Vaccine_and_the_R
ehr_evidence: Eligible Kansas guardians of children aged 9 - 17 years completed an online survey.
summary: Cross-sectional survey study assessing Kansas guardians' perceptions of HPV and the HPV vaccine, and the influence of social media messages on those perceptions and vaccination decisions.
key_findings: 57.9% (n=55) of guardians reported seeing information about HPV and the HPV vaccine on social media.

Guardians who saw HPV vaccine information on social media were significantly more likely to perceive the vaccine could kill their child compared to those who did not (M=2.50, SD=1.62 vs M=1.74, SD=0.85; t(79)=0.019).
Children of guardians with annual household income ≥$100,000 were significantly more likely to have received at least one HPV vaccine dose than children of guardians earning <$100,000 (p=0.003).
Higher HPV vaccine harm perception scores significantly predicted lower effectiveness perception scores (β=-0.451, R=0.620, F[1,57]=35.63, p<0.0001), explaining 38.5% of the variance.
captured_features: Demographic characteristics (sex, age, race, education, income, region)
Social media use and exposure to HPV/HPV vaccine information
Perception scales (susceptibility, severity, benefits, barriers, cues to action, self-efficacy)
population: Kansas guardians of children aged 9-17 years
exposure_domain: Social media messages about HPV and HPV vaccine
limitations: Convenience sampling with a small, non-representative sample (n=95)
Self-reported vaccination status and perceptions subject to recall and social desirability bias
Limited generalizability to other regions or demographics
